title: Screening for Prediabetes and Type 2 Diabetes
text: The USPSTF recommends screening for prediabetes and type 2 diabetes in adults aged 35 to 70 years who have overweight or obesity. Clinicians should offer or refer patients with prediabetes to effective preventive interventions.

title: Screening for Prediabetes and Type 2 Diabetes
text: Screening every 3 years may be a reasonable approach for adults with normal blood glucose levels.

title: Statin Use for the Primary Prevention of Cardiovascular Disease in Adults: Preventive Medication
text: The USPSTF recommends that clinicians prescribe a statin for the primary prevention of CVD for adults aged 40 to 75 years who have 1 or more CVD risk factors (i.e. dyslipidemia, diabetes, hypertension, or smoking) and an estimated 10-year risk of a cardiovascular event of 10% or greater.

title: Statin Use for the Primary Prevention of Cardiovascular Disease in Adults: Preventive Medication
section: Recommendation Summary - Adults 40-75y, 10-year risk 7.5% to <10% (Grade C)
text: The USPSTF recommends that clinicians selectively offer a statin for the primary prevention of CVD for adults aged 40 to 75 years who have 1 or more CVD risk factors (i.e dyslipidemia, diabetes, hypertension, or smoking) and an estimated 10-year risk of a cardiovascular event of 7.5% to less than 10%. The likelihood of benefit is smaller in this group than in persons with a 10-year risk of 10% or greater.

title: Statin Use for the Primary Prevention of Cardiovascular Disease in Adults: Preventive Medication
section: Recommendation Summary - Adults 76 years or older (Grade I)
text: The USPSTF concludes that the current evidence is insufficient to assess the balance of benefits and harms of initiating a statin for the primary prevention of CVD events and mortality in adults 76 years or older.

title: Hypertension in Adults: Screening
text: The USPSTF recommends screening for hypertension in adults 18 years or older with office blood pressure measurement (OBPM). The USPSTF recommends obtaining blood pressure measurements outside of the clinical setting for diagnostic confirmation before starting treatment.

title: Hypertension in Adults: Screening
text: The USPSTF suggests annual screening for hypertension in adults 40 years or older and for adults at increased risk for hypertension (such as Black persons, persons with high-normal blood pressure, or persons who are overweight or obese). Screening less frequently (ie, every 3 to 5 years) is appropriate for adults aged 18 to 39 years not at increased risk for hypertension and with a prior normal blood pressure reading.

title: A1C Test for Diabetes and Prediabetes
text: The A1C test measures the percentage of your red blood cells that have sugar-coated hemoglobin.

title: A1C Test for Diabetes and Prediabetes
text:
The following ranges are used to diagnose prediabetes and diabetes:
Normal: below 5.7%
Prediabetes: 5.7% to 6.4%
Diabetes: 6.5% or above

title: A1C Test for Diabetes and Prediabetes
text: Get an A1C test if you're over age 45. A1C testing is also recommended if you're younger, have overweight, and any other risk factor for prediabetes and type 2 diabetes

title: The Surprising Truth About Prediabetes
text: People with prediabetes have higher blood sugar than normal, but not high enough yet for a diabetes diagnosis.

title: The Surprising Truth About Prediabetes
text: You can have prediabetes for years without symptoms. This means you likely won't know you have prediabetes until serious health problems show up. Talk to your doctor about getting your blood sugar tested if you have any risk factors, including: Having overweight. Being 45 years or older. Having a parent, brother, or sister with type 2 diabetes.

title: About High Blood Pressure
text: Blood pressure is the pressure that occurs when blood pushes against the walls of your arteries. Arteries carry blood from your heart to other parts of your body.

title: About High Blood Pressure
text: High blood pressure usually has no warning signs or symptoms, and many people do not know they have it.

title: Medication Safety and Your Health
text: Medicines are safe when used as prescribed or as directed on the label. There are risks in taking any medicine, vitamin or other supplement. An adverse drug event (ADE) is when a medication causes harm to someone.

title: Medication Safety and Your Health
text: Keep a list of your medicines, vitamins, and other supplements. Make sure your doctor knows about all the medicines, vitamins and other supplements you take.

title: Diabetes Tests & Diagnosis
text: Your doctor can diagnose diabetes , prediabetes , and gestational diabetes using blood tests. The blood tests show if your blood glucose level , also called blood sugar, is higher than the range that is healthy for you.

title: The A1C Test & Diabetes
section: What Is the A1C Test Used For?
text: The A1C test can be used to diagnose type 2 diabetes and prediabetes . 1 The A1C test is also the primary test used for diabetes management

title: The A1C Test & Diabetes
section: How Often Should I Get an A1C Test?
text: Experts recommend that people with diabetes have an A1C test at least twice a year.

title: Laboratory Evaluation of Kidney Disease
text: Laboratory measurement and reporting are critical to promoting early detection and management of chronic kidney disease (CKD).

title: Blood Cholesterol
text: Cholesterol is a waxy, fat-like substance that your body needs for good health, but in the right amounts.

title: Blood Cholesterol
text: High levels of "bad" LDL cholesterol may create a buildup of plaque

title: Blood Cholesterol - Diagnosis
text: Your healthcare provider will diagnose you with high blood cholesterol based on your medical and family history, a physical exam, and a blood test of your cholesterol levels.

title: Blood Cholesterol - Diagnosis
text: A lipoprotein panel, also called a lipid panel or lipid profile, measures the levels of LDL and HDL cholesterol and triglycerides

title: High Blood Pressure - Symptoms
text: Blood pressure this high can damage your organs. If your blood pressure is 180/120 but you don't have symptoms, wait 5 minutes and check your blood pressure again. If it is still high, call your healthcare provider who may recommend starting a medicine or changing your dose.

title: Prediabetes
text: Prediabetes means that your blood glucose, or blood sugar , levels are higher than normal but not high enough to be called diabetes

title: Hemoglobin A1C (HbA1c) Test
text: A hemoglobin A1C (HbA1C) test is a blood test that shows your average level of blood glucose , also called blood sugar, over the past two to three months

title: Hemoglobin A1C (HbA1c) Test
text: A1C results tell you what percentage of your hemoglobin is coated with glucose.

title: Cholesterol Levels
text: A cholesterol test is a blood test that measures the amount of cholesterol and triglycerides (a type of fat) in your blood.

title: Cholesterol Levels
text: In general, low LDL levels and high HDL cholesterol levels are good for heart health.

title: High Blood Pressure
text: Blood pressure is the force of your blood pushing against the walls of your arteries.

title: Complete Blood Count (CBC)
text: Abnormal levels of red blood cells, hemoglobin, or hematocrit may be a sign of dehydration , anemia, heart disease , or too little iron in your body

title: Kidney Tests
text: Kidney tests check to see how well your kidneys are working. They include blood, urine , and imaging tests

title: Kidney Tests
text: Early kidney disease usually does not have signs or symptoms. Testing is the only way to know how your kidneys are doing.

title: Kidney Tests
text: It is important for you to get checked for kidney disease if you have the key risk factors - diabetes, high blood pressure, heart disease, or a family history of kidney failure.

title: Creatinine Test
text: This test measures creatinine levels in a sample of your blood and/or urine (pee). Creatinine is a normal waste product in your body. It's made when you use your muscles and some of the muscle tissue breaks down. Normally, your kidneys filter creatinine from your blood and remove it from your body in your urine

title: Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR) Test
text: A GFR test checks for kidney disease by measuring how much blood your kidneys filter each minute.

title: Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR) Test
text: A normal eGFR means that you probably don't have kidney disease. An eGFR that's below normal or low may mean that you may have kidney disease. A very low eGFR means that you may have kidney failure.

title: Iron-Deficiency Anemia
text: Iron-deficiency anemia is a type of anemia that develops if you do not have enough iron in your body. It is the most common type of anemia.

title: Iron-Deficiency Anemia
text: People with mild or moderate iron-deficiency anemia may not have any symptoms. More serious iron-deficiency anemia may cause common symptoms of anemia, such as tiredness, shortness of breath, or chest pain. Other symptoms include: Fatigue Dizziness or lightheadedness Cold hands and feet Pale skin

title: Anemia
text: Some types of anemias are caused by factors you can't change, like your family history or your age. Other anemias are caused by factors you can manage, like eating habits or other health conditions that control how your body makes red blood cells.

title: Medicines
text: Medicines can treat diseases and improve your health. If you are like most people, you need to take medicine at some point in your life.
